newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Germany's Kinkel denies any rift with Waigel.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kinkel denies any rift with Waigel.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel denied on Wednesday any rift with cabinet colleague Theo Waigel after the finance minister had accused him of meddling in policy issues that did not concern him.
"My relations with Waigel are good. It is not worth worrying about this," Kinkel told a news conference here when asked to comment on Waigel's remarks.
Waigel had lashed out at Kinkel over statements he made earlier this week about economic and monetary union (EMU).
"I advise my colleague Kinkel and other European foreign ministers to stick to their own task of political union and spare us their advice about currency union," Waigel said.

The finance minister was angered by Kinkel's suggestion that EMU had "passed the point of no return" and implied a certain flexibility in interpreting the entry tests by saying they were a "process" rather than targets to be hit on a certain day.
The clash was seen as a sign of strain within the ruling three-party coalition of German Chancellor Helmut Kohl.

On a one-day visit to Lisbon for talks with his Portuguese counterpart Jaime Gama, Kinkel reaffirmed his confidence that Germany would succeed in getting its economy into shape for the launch of the single currency in January 1999.
"We want to be inside (monetary union). I believe we will make the criteria," he said.
The two foreign ministers ministers discussed issues ranging from Nato enlargement to European Union plans to reform its workings ahead of the planned inclusion of new members.
